stories.head: Trump called anyone saying artificial intelligence, not superintelligence, the enemy.
stories.body: The US president posted it a week after ordering federal agencies to use his term. He cannot make private people use it, and superintelligence already means AI beyond human ability.

stories.head: Japan's prime minister replied to Trump that Japan will keep saying AI for now.
stories.body: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi answered US President Trump's UN call last month to say superintelligence. She told parliament the word AI fills official papers, and she will watch other governments.

stories.head: Elon Musk accused Indian tycoons of blocking Starlink; India's government denies it.
stories.body: Musk, who runs SpaceX and its Starlink satellite internet, says Starlink has waited five years. India's ministry says Starlink and two rivals all await security clearance, calling the claim baseless.

stories.head: OpenAI told investors its yearly sales pace is $20 billion below what it said before.
stories.body: An unnamed source says the gap is mostly a counting difference with rival Anthropic. Anthropic counts cloud partner sales, OpenAI does not, and a pace is not money earned.

stories.head: The World Trade Organization doubled its 2026 trade forecast, crediting the AI boom.
stories.body: Trade in AI goods like chips and servers rose two thirds in the first half. Those goods gave almost half of all trade growth, outweighing the Middle East war's damage.

stories.head: Anthropic now scans open-source software, code anyone can read, for flaws for free.
stories.body: Projects that opt in get regular scans by its strongest models, with no human review. Anthropic says some may be wrong, and some projects already drown in AI bug reports.

stories.head: OpenAI shut down Russian and Iranian groups that used ChatGPT to invent journalists.
stories.body: One invented a think-tank head, the other placed almost 100 articles under fake names. OpenAI names no government agency behind either, and the whole account is its own investigation.

stories.head: Oracle is trucking natural gas to its AI data centres while it waits for pipelines.
stories.body: Trucked gas ran a Utah site a year and now feeds a Texas OpenAI campus. Analysts put trucked gas at about four times the usual price; Oracle did not comment.

stories.head: Humanoid robots directed traffic and guided tourists on busy streets in Hangzhou.
stories.body: Robot maker Deep Robotics says its DR02 robots worked junctions in heavy traffic and rain. It aims to free staff for judgment work, but only the maker describes the trial.

stories.head: Walmart's warehouse robots break down too often and cannot handle its big boxes.
stories.body: Walmart is still automating most of its roughly 200 US supply buildings after a decade. Executives say fewer warehouse workers will be needed in time, but promise no layoffs.

stories.head: Google unveiled its new top AI model, Gemini 4 Argon, for cyber defenders first.
stories.body: Those defenders get it without the usual cyber safeguards; paying developers follow after safety tests. Google claims leading scores in coding, finance, law and security, all measured by itself.

stories.head: Scientists call Anthropic's claim that its AI found a gene-editing tool overstated.
stories.body: Anthropic said last month its AI agents found a DNA pattern that may edit genes. Copenhagen researcher Mario Rodríguez Mestre says his unpublished work shows it; he cannot prove copying.

stories.head: USA Today's publisher sued OpenAI for copying hundreds of thousands of its articles.
stories.body: The publisher and its local papers say OpenAI trained on their articles without asking. They seek over $250 million, joining The New York Times; OpenAI had not responded.

stories.head: A Google chatbot questioned patients before urgent visits and needed no safety stop.
stories.body: Boston hospital doctors watched all 98 completed chats live and never had to step in. The study, paid by Google's parent, tested only safety, not whether patients got better.

stories.head: A US charity plans to record Gaza classrooms and have AI flag 'hateful' speech.
stories.body: Gaza Children Village founder Dr David Hasan described the plan in a webinar last month. A board member and a partner aid group raised concerns, and families may not know.

stories.head: A Colombian streamer's own robot whacked him on the head during a livestream.
stories.body: Streamer Westcol turned his back while rehearsing a dance with the robot on air. He says it cost about $100,000 and had already kicked a display case to bits.

teaser.head: Google unveiled one Gemini agent for businesses that works across apps and devices.
A humanoid shop robot shown in Tokyo could stock Japanese convenience stores from 2027.
Democratic senators say big tech misleads the public on AI data centre costs and jobs.
The AI boom drove San Francisco rents up a quarter; eviction notices rose 44 percent.

bp.head: AI investors began paying for proof, not plans, after OpenAI's lower sales number.
bp.body: OpenAI gave investors a lower sales pace; data-centre firm Firmus shelved its listing. Watch OpenAI's $1.4 trillion round, a sector test; not financial advice.
